questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Low shoulder.
No parking at any time.
Lane ends.

questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to stay in the right lane. It warns you about a hazard ahead.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.
Signal only if there is visible traffic.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only when driving in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Do not skip signaling just because you do not see other cars. This is the law.

questions.question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow the directions indicated by the traffic light.
Follow the directions given by the officer.
Honk at the officer.
Check to see what the cars next to them are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the officer.
questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, follow their directions instead of the traffic light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield just to the traffic on the right.
Yield just to the traffic on the left.
Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and let other traffic go first. You do not have to stop unless traffic is coming.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:

options.text: Use your signal.
Turn the wheel.
Increase your speed.
Change lanes.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal three to four seconds before you turn.

questions.question: A telltale sign of a drunk driver is:

options.text: They are weaving between lanes.
They are driving more slowly than the normal traffic flow.
They are making quick and sudden stops.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include weaving between lanes, driving too slow, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Make no driving errors.
Have trouble driving slowly.
Are better drivers because they are not hungry.
Have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. This makes it harder to control your car and stay in your lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.
No left turn.

questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: Seat belts are most effective when they are worn by:

options.text: The person driving the car.
Passengers when they are on a long drive.
All occupants of a car being driven on an expressway.
All occupants of a car every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: All occupants of a car every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in your car should wear a seat belt every time you drive. Without a seat belt, a person can be thrown around during a crash.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Keep your tires properly maintained.
Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch out for standing water or puddles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, cars need more distance to stop. Slow down, avoid cruise control, and watch for puddles. Keep your tires in good condition.

questions.question: What should you do to make sure your physical condition does not cause unsafe driving?

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular physical exams.
Know how any medicine you take affects your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects how safely you can drive. Know your physical limits and only drive when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: How can you help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?

options.text: Allow extra time for your trip.
Follow posted speed limits.
Use your turn signals properly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your drive.

questions.question: A driver ahead of you is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Stay a safe distance behind them.
Understand that this driver is not paying full attention to the road.
Do not drive the same way.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space because they are more likely to cause an accident.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for trucks.
Do not pass trucks.
Truck parking area ahead.
Steep downgrade ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that there is a steep hill coming up ahead.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. When must you stop?

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is lowered.
If the crossing lights are flashing.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop before crossing railroad tracks if red lights are flashing, a gate is lowered, a stop sign is posted, a person signals you to stop, or a train is visible or close enough to be dangerous. Never race a train.

questions.question: Where is passing another car not allowed?

options.text: On hills and curves.
At intersections.
At railroad crossings.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: It is illegal and unsafe to pass another car on hills, curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.

questions.question: Why is night driving harder than daytime driving?

options.text: Cars overheat faster at night.
It is harder to see in the dark.
Rain is more likely at night.
You are more likely to see a motorcycle at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is harder to see in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Always use proper headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: Another vehicle is following you too closely. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard.
Get behind them and turn on your high beams.
Tap your brakes lightly, slow down, and let them pass.
Drive slowly and prevent them from passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes lightly, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If someone is following too closely, tap your brakes lightly to alert them, then slow down to let them pass. If needed, pull over and stop to let them go by.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Signal your lane change.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When changing lanes, signal early, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.
When turning left or right.
When changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you change your vehicle's position. Look over your shoulder when turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lowering your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions affect how well you drive. If you are worried, excited, afraid, angry, or sad, you may not drive safely. Stress makes it hard to concentrate on driving. Wait to drive until you feel calm.

questions.question: To help relieve fatigue on a long trip, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: On long trips, stop every two hours for a short break to avoid fatigue. If you feel drowsy, pull over to a safe place and take a nap or spend the night in a room.

questions.question: Pedestrians must:

options.text: Use crosswalks at intersections.
Look both ways before crossing the street.
Obey "Walk" and "Don't Walk" signals.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians must use crosswalks at intersections, look both ways before crossing, and obey all "Walk" and "Don't Walk" signs. Drivers must yield to pedestrians who are crossing.

questions.question: To change lanes you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal first. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one is entering the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: When you need to change lanes, it is important to:

options.text: Signal your intentions before the lane change.
Check your blind spot.
Make sure the lane is clear before entering.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal for enough time before changing lanes or exiting. Turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.
